M01.note: Overt reading inherited from the Chang-lab ECoG paradigm; nothing new here.

M02.note: Inferred articulation inherited from Chartier et al. 2018, and it smuggles phoneme-label supervision into the stage-1 target.

M03.note: Per-participant training with early stopping is ordinary for invasive decoding.

choice: Applied to 58 mimed trials of 10 sentences (P1)
M04.note: Same audible-to-silent design as Martin et al. 2014, with mimed values only in figures and conflicting n, so the transfer is shown against chance but not quantified.

M05.note: Standard clinical high-density ECoG features of the lineage.

M06.note: First implementation of a neural-to-articulatory-to-acoustic decoder, but the gain over direct decoding is one participant and confounded by extra phonetic supervision, and later work found direct decoding as good, so not ahead.

M07.field: No language model or lexicon at use time
M07.note: Direct acoustic synthesis needs no language model.

M08.note: Sentence waveforms with listener tests extend earlier formant and spectrogram decoding; the offline MLSA result is now far behind instantaneous intracortical synthesis.

M11.note: Session-wise split is sound, but the Fig. 1 caption's 5-fold cross-validation contradicts Methods.

M12.field: Listener intelligibility tests of synthesized speech
M12.note: Listener transcription was established practice, and closed word pools without a chance-level WER make this paper's intelligibility numbers uninterpretable.

M13.note: Temporary clinical ECoG with code and data on request is typical of invasive studies.
